analysis:
Reviewed .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml: base excerpt (lines 1049-1523) and head excerpt (lines 1-532). The visible changes are CI plumbing: a new required `cluster_gpu` input (head line 14), build jobs now run only when `inputs.cluster`/`inputs.provider` is 'true' (head lines 60, 178; the push-with-skip cache-refresh path is removed), and the test-cluster-gpu section and gate/record edits (changed ranges around 916-923 and 1514-1539) fall outside the supplied excerpts, so I could not view them.

Security-relevant observations:
- Workflow permissions remain `contents: read`, and actions stay pinned by SHA.
- The `.git` cache hardening (discarding symlinks, hooks, and fsmonitor/hooksPath/include config; fsck) is unchanged.
- SAVE_CACHES is still limited to push on master/dev or dispatch on dev, so PRs cannot poison caches.
- Removing the build-on-skipped-push path only reduces cache-save activity; it adds no new attack surface.
- The gate requires exact job results, and the diff does not appear to weaken it. The head-side gate (including any added cluster-gpu expectations) is not visible, so this is unverified.
- No provider runtime assets or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041) are touched by the visible hunks; the T-041 cache text in the context concerns provider code, not this CI file.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that the head provider-test-gate still fails when test-cluster-gpu or other required jobs are skipped or unexpectedly run, and that the new `cluster_gpu` input is supplied by every caller (ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml).
